episodes.title: In 1956, the future kitchen looked like this
episodes.headline:
THE FUTURE KITCHEN
ACCORDING TO 1956

beats.text: In 1956, the kitchen of tomorrow came with a recipe screen. The touchscreen? Not included.
In this General Motors promotional fantasy, you insert a card, see the dish, and let the push-button spectacle begin.
The mixer drops from a cabinet. The refrigerator puts its contents on a rotating display.
Even the oven opens like a tiny spaceship. Subtle? Absolutely not.
The promise wasn't just dinner. It was freedom from housework, with time left over for fun.
They imagined a kitchen that performed for you. Somehow, we still ended up arguing about who loads the dishwasher.

episodes.title: The smart kitchen before apps existed
episodes.headline:
SMART KITCHEN?
TRY 1956.

beats.text: Forget downloading a recipe app. This imagined kitchen wanted you to insert a card.
Design for Dreaming, a 1956 promotional film, turns cooking into a parade of buttons, screens, and moving appliances.
Notice the trick: the complicated work seems to disappear into the cabinets.
The food itself becomes a display. Even opening the fridge looks like a product launch.
This isn't a documentary about an ordinary home. It's a carefully staged dream of convenience.
The gadgets look strange today. But the sales pitch sounds familiar: buy the future, and get your time back.
